chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Abu Jamila, from Mu'adh ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed the Testament descended from the heavens upon Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) as an Ordinance — there did not descend upon Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) any sealed Ordinance except the Testament. So Jibra'il (peace be upon him) said: 'O Muhammad! This is your testament regarding your community, which is with the People of your Household.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Which of the People of my Household, O Jibra'il?' He said: 'The noble one of Allah among them and his offspring, so that they may inherit from you the knowledge of prophethood just as Ibrahim (peace be upon him) made it to be inherited, and its inheritance is for Ali (peace be upon him) and your offspring from his lineage.'

He said: And there were seals upon it. He said: So Ali (peace be upon him) opened the first seal and carried out what was therein. Then al-Hasan (peace be upon him) opened the second seal and carried out what he had been commanded therein. When al-Hasan passed away and departed, al-Husayn (peace be upon him) opened the third seal and found therein: 'Fight! So kill and be killed, and go out with groups of people for martyrdom — there is no martyrdom for them except with you.' He said: So he (peace be upon him) did it. When he departed, he handed it over to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) before that. He opened the fourth seal and found therein: 'Be silent and withhold, for knowledge has been veiled.'

So when he passed away and departed, he handed it over to Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him). He opened the fifth seal and found therein: 'Interpret the Book of Allah the Exalted, and affirm your father, and make your son inherit, and cultivate the community, and uphold the right of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and speak the truth in fear and security, and do not fear except Allah.' So he did it. Then he handed it over to the one who follows him. He (Mu'adh) said: I said to him: 'May I be your sacrifice — are you him?' He said: 'My only concern, O Mu'adh, is that you will go and report against me.' He said: So I said: 'I ask Allah, Who granted you this rank from your forefathers, that He grant you from your offspring the like of it before death.' He said: 'Allah has already done so, O Mu'adh.'

He said: 'Allah has already done so, O Mu'adh.' He said: So I said: 'Who is that, may I be your sacrifice?' He said: 'This sleeping one,' and he gestured with his hand toward al-'Abd al-Salih (the seventh Imam), who was sleeping.

key_terms.العبد الصالح: The righteous servant — a title for Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the Divine Testament (al-Wasiyya) and how was it transmitted to each Imam in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates a tradition about the Divine Testament (al-Wasiyya) which descended from the heavens to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) as a sealed ordinance. The Imam describes how each Imam in succession opened one seal of the Testament and carried out its specific command — Imam Ali was commanded to transmit knowledge, Imam al-Hasan to act on his command, Imam al-Husayn to fight and embrace martyrdom, Imam Zayn al-'Abidin to remain silent while knowledge was veiled, and Imam al-Baqir to interpret the Book of Allah, affirm his father, and speak truth without fear. The narrative concludes with Imam al-Sadiq revealing that the next Imam (Imam Musa al-Kazim) was already designated, pointing to the sleeping child — affirming the divine continuity of the Imamate and its pre-ordained nature.
